controls.title: Harden user applications
controls.statement: Apply and maintain approved security settings for office suites, PDF software and web browsers using ASD or vendor guidance.
controls.risk: A malicious document or website could exploit weak application settings to steal information or compromise a user device.
controls.scope: Office productivity suites, PDF software, web browsers and their extensions; macro execution is assessed under OM controls.
controls.examine: Compare deployed application settings, versions and extensions with approved hardening standards and exception records.
controls.interview: Ask application owners how baselines are selected, tested, deployed and updated after product or threat changes.
controls.test: Inspect representative managed devices and verify required settings and extension restrictions cannot be bypassed by a standard user.
test_steps: Select representative managed devices, user roles, browsers, office applications, PDF readers and installed extensions or plug-ins.
Inspect effective policy for approved hardening settings and compare it with the device baseline and central compliance report.
Using a standard user, attempt to change protected settings, install an unapproved extension and enable a prohibited feature in a test profile.
Confirm changes are denied or reverted, deviations are detected centrally and supported business exceptions are narrowly scoped and current.
controls.expected: In-scope applications apply current approved security settings, restrict unapproved extensions and record justified exceptions.

mappings.basis: Requires office productivity suites to be hardened using ASD or vendor guidance.
Requires PDF software to be hardened using ASD or vendor guidance.
Requires web browsers to be hardened using ASD or vendor guidance.
Requires browser and email-client extensions to be restricted to authorised extensions.

controls.title: Block unsafe application behaviour
controls.statement: Prevent user applications from launching child processes, executing embedded content, injecting code or using other unnecessary high-risk functions.
controls.risk: An attacker could turn a trusted office or PDF application into a pathway for running malicious code on the device.
controls.scope: User applications and risky functions other than Microsoft Office macro execution, which is assessed under OM controls.
controls.examine: Inspect managed policies for child processes, executable content, code injection, OLE packages and user-change restrictions.
controls.interview: Ask application and security owners how risky functions are identified and how business exceptions are constrained.
controls.test: Use safe test documents to confirm blocked process creation, executable content, code injection and prohibited embedded packages.
test_steps: Prepare safe documents and browser content that attempt representative prohibited behaviours such as child-process creation, executable content, code injection or unsafe embedded packages.
Open each sample with standard-user applications in an isolated representative environment and verify the behaviour is blocked before execution.
Try benign delivery variations such as archive, rename, alternate application or user-writable location to confirm enforcement follows behaviour and origin.
Trace prevention events into monitoring with file, process, user, device and rule context, then remove artefacts and restore the test environment.
controls.expected: Prohibited behaviours are blocked and logged, users cannot weaken the settings, and approved exceptions are narrow and reviewed.

mappings.basis: Requires office productivity suites to be prevented from creating child processes.
Requires office productivity suites to be prevented from creating executable content.
Requires office productivity suites to be prevented from injecting code into other processes.
Requires activation of Object Linking and Embedding packages to be prevented.
Prevents users from changing specified web-browser security settings.
